name: Valongo Wharf Archaeological Site
description: Beneath a square in Rio de Janeiro's old port lies the stone wharf where enslaved Africans were landed from 1811 onwards. Archaeologists uncovered its layers of paving, including the rough "pé de moleque" stonework of the original quay. An estimated 900,000 people arrived here, making it the most important physical trace of that history in the Americas.
